svg.title: The toolbox checks the test really failed first, instead of taking anyone's word for it: A project generated by the toolbox can prove its own failing test
svg.text: The toolbox checks the test really failed first, instead
of taking anyone's word for it
Scenario: A project generated by the toolbox can prove its own failing test
The same proof, in a generated project

g.text: Given a generated project copies the CodeceptJS sample and writes a test that cannot pass
This is a project generated by the toolbox, not the toolbox itself. The developer copies the CodeceptJS sample it ships
into project/tests/application/, the folder its CodeceptJS tasks point at, and writes a first test.
git status lists the three new files: the copied sample and the two test files, shown line by line below it. The test
asks for a greeting the project cannot give yet, so it is meant to fail.
When the generated project runs that test and it fails on what it checks
The test runs with the copied sample and fails on what it checks: "expected 'Hello, Lambda', got ''", exit code 1.
The sample also writes a report of that run: the report folder now holds results-1.xml.
Then the generated project's own check accepts that failure as proof
The same check as in the toolbox's own loop, typed in the generated project with no folder to point it at. The line task
prints shows where it looks by default: REPORT_DIR=project/tests/application/_output/junit, the folder the sample writes
It finds the report there and accepts the failure: "The failure is real", and it quotes the check that failed.
